title: Give an emotional word visible weight and a lower resting place

motion.summary: CAIN WAS arrives high, DEEPLY occupies the next level, and the broad red GRIEVED settles on the lowest tier.
phases: Build the subject and modifier on successively lower tiers.
Place the heaviest, widest emotional word at the bottom and hold the completed reading.
motion.transferablePrinciple: Use size, weight and vertical ordering to make emotional pressure visible without requiring illustrative footage.
variations: Make a fragile word deform a solid platform instead of adding decorative lines.
Reverse the gravity for relief, forgiveness or hope.
Let a single object descend while the sentence remains stable around it.
cautions: Do not use downward motion as a generic entrance for unrelated words.
Replace the shelf-line motif if nearby scenes already use line fields.
Preserve semantic reading order across the vertical layout.

quality.reviewer: agent visual inspection of decoded frame sequence
strengths: The red emphasis and larger word mass immediately identify the emotional center.
The descending three-tier composition is readable in the inspected samples.
limitations: The sequence is short and much of the latter half is a reading hold.
The samples show position states; they do not establish physical bounce or a measured gravity curve.
Observed from six decoded frames of the exact hashed MP4; this is a concept reference, not full motion, audio-sync or whole-film acceptance.
